Many investors ask me how our rules are made, so let me explain the process. First, a draft is written by our technical team. Then it is published for public consultation, usually for forty-five days. Last year, our tariff rule received more than four hundred comments. All of them were read, and the main ones were answered in a report. After that, the text was amended and the final rule was approved by the board. The new requirements will be enforced from January. So, when you read a rule from our agency, remember that it was discussed in public before it was published.

Three years ago, a new rule for port terminals was published by the agency. Our client believed that one requirement was illegal, so the rule was taken to court. The first judge disagreed with us, and the rule was enforced for eight months. Then the case was sent to a higher court, and the ruling was overturned. The old framework was applied again. For my client, that was good news. For the investors in the sector, it was terrible, because nobody knew which rule would be applied next year. Since then, the rule has been amended twice, and it is still being discussed.
